claude.performance_metric: no divestiture; held ~8 years, re-IPO October 2015
claude.rationale: Per section 2, this was a whole-company going-concern LBO: product (T4), processes (T5), and organization/people (T6) all transferred together intact, with the only immediate change being capital structure (new senior secured credit agreement), so no product-vs-process (gap_45=0) or process-vs-organization (gap_56=0) mismatch at closing. Section 4 explicitly documents "None documented" for both P4 (product and operating processes moved together intact; merchant attrition was competitive/market-driven) and P5 (operations and people moved together as a going concern), yielding p4_pathway=0 and p5_pathway=0. The controlling-principal archetype shifted from public-company operator to KKR financial sponsor with a balance-sheet-first thesis that became the primary channel of subsequent strain (t1_archetype=1), while section 4 documents no business-model incompatibility (t2_model=0).

gemini.performance_metric: no divestiture; held for about eight years before 2015 IPO
gemini.rationale: The dossier documents a whole-company going-concern LBO where all operational tiers (T4, T5, T6) transferred intact and together. Consequently, there were no structural gaps at the product-process (gap_45) or process-organization (gap_56) interfaces. Post-deal strain was driven by capital structure and macro timing, with no documented operational disruption at the T4/T5 (p4_pathway) or T5/T6 (p5_pathway) boundaries.

grok.rationale: gap_45=0 and p4_pathway=0 per section 2 T4/T5 (product franchise and operating processes transferred together intact as going concern) and section 4 P4 (none documented; merchant attrition was market-driven). gap_56=0 and p5_pathway=0 per section 2 T5/T6 (people transferred with going concern) and section 4 P5 (none documented). T1 replace and T2 1-1 drawn directly from section 2 lines on public-to-KKR sponsor shift and retained payment-processing model.
